sdk.name: Chat apps with the Foundry SDK

questions.q: A loan-approval model approves noticeably fewer applicants from one state, even when income and credit history are identical. Which responsible AI principle does this violate?
questions.e: Treating people in similar situations differently is a fairness issue.

questions.q: A bank publishes a document describing what its AI assistant can and cannot do, and tells customers when they are chatting with AI. Which principle does this support?
questions.e: Helping people understand how a system works and its limits is transparency.

questions.q: A company sets up a review board that owns its AI models, audits their decisions and can override them. Which principle is this?
questions.e: Accountability means people are responsible for AI systems, with governance and human oversight.

questions.q: An AI app adds screen-reader support, captions and voice input in regional languages. Which principle is addressed?
questions.e: Inclusiveness means empowering everyone, including people with disabilities and speakers of different languages.

questions.q: A healthcare chatbot is tested on rare and unusual symptoms before launch, and hands over to a doctor whenever it is unsure. Which principle?
questions.e: Reliability and safety: the system behaves correctly in unexpected conditions and fails safely.

questions.q: Customer voice recordings used to improve a model are encrypted, access-controlled and deleted after 90 days. Which principle?
questions.e: Protecting personal data and controlling its use is privacy and security.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
o: Providing reason codes for a declined credit application supports transparency.
Making an app usable with a screen reader supports fairness.
Human review of high-impact AI decisions supports accountability.
questions.e: Reason codes explain the decision (transparency). Screen-reader support is inclusiveness, not fairness. Human oversight is accountability.

questions.q: Match each scenario to the responsible AI principle it addresses.
o: A CV screener is tested for different outcomes by gender
A chatbot discloses that it is an AI
Personal data is anonymised before training
An AI tutor works for students with low vision
questions.e: Equal outcomes → fairness; disclosure → transparency; protecting data → privacy and security; access for everyone → inclusiveness.

questions.q: Which principle is MOST directly supported by applying content filters that block harmful outputs from a generative model?
questions.e: Content filters prevent harmful behaviour, which is part of reliability and safety.

questions.q: An AI system must keep working correctly when users type misspelled or unusual inputs. Which principle?
questions.e: Robustness to unexpected input is reliability and safety.

questions.q: Which TWO actions improve the transparency of an AI-based credit decision system? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
o: Explain the main factors behind each decision to the applicant
Document the model’s intended use and known limitations
Encrypt the training data at rest
Translate the app into more languages
questions.e: Explanations and documentation help people understand the system. Encryption is privacy; translation is inclusiveness.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: Ensuring that a named team is responsible for an AI system’s outcomes and can intervene is an example of ______.
questions.e: Ownership and the ability to intervene are accountability.

questions.q: A face-blurring feature for CCTV footage is added so bystanders cannot be identified. Which principle?
questions.e: Protecting people’s identities is privacy.

questions.q: A hiring company uses an AI model to rank candidates. For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
o: Checking whether rankings differ by gender for similar profiles is a fairness consideration.
Letting a recruiter override the ranking is an accountability consideration.
Storing candidates’ CVs without consent is acceptable if the model is accurate.
questions.e: Group-outcome checks are fairness; human override is accountability; accuracy never excuses misuse of personal data (privacy).

questions.q: Which practice BEST reduces the risk of a generative model inventing facts in a customer-facing answer?
o: Ground the model with trusted company documents and ask it to cite them
Use a larger max tokens value
questions.e: Grounding (RAG) gives the model real data to rely on; higher temperature makes inventions more likely.

questions.q: An insurance chatbot is offered in Hindi, Tamil and Bengali so more customers can use it. Which principle?
questions.e: Broadening access across languages is inclusiveness.

questions.q: Which principle is concerned with an AI system resisting attacks such as prompt injection and data theft?
questions.e: Security against misuse and attacks falls under privacy and security.

questions.q: Match each Foundry or process feature to the principle it mainly supports.
o: Content filters on a model deployment
Role-based access control on the project
An approval step before an agent issues a refund
questions.e: Filters prevent harm; documentation explains; RBAC protects data and access; human approval keeps people responsible.

questions.q: A model performs well for urban customers but poorly for rural customers because rural data was scarce in training. Which principle is at risk FIRST?
questions.e: Unequal performance across groups is a fairness problem, often caused by unrepresentative data.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a human-in-the-loop review for low-confidence AI outputs?
o: To keep people responsible for decisions and catch errors before they cause harm
To make the model respond faster
questions.e: Human review supports accountability and reliability.

questions.q: What is a token in the context of large language models?
o: A unit of text, such as a word or part of a word, that the model processes
A security key used to call the model
questions.e: Models read and write text as tokens; limits and pricing are counted in tokens.

questions.q: Which statement BEST describes how a language model generates a response?
o: It predicts the next token repeatedly, based on the probabilities learned in training
It retrieves a stored answer from a database of questions
It runs a fixed set of if-then rules
It searches the internet for each answer
questions.e: LLMs generate text one token at a time by predicting likely next tokens.

questions.q: What does a model’s context window define?
o: The maximum number of tokens the model can consider in one request, including the output
The number of users who can call the model at once
The time limit for a response
The size of the training dataset
questions.e: The context window includes the system prompt, history, added data and the generated answer.

questions.q: You need consistent, repeatable answers when extracting fields from support emails. How should you set temperature?
o: Temperature has no effect on output
questions.e: Low temperature makes output more deterministic and focused.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: The ______ parameter limits the length of the generated response.
questions.e: Max (output) tokens caps the response length and cost.

questions.q: Which type of model should you choose for semantic search over thousands of documents?
o: A reasoning model with high reasoning effort
questions.e: Embedding models convert text to vectors so similar meanings can be found.

questions.q: A mobile app must run a small model with low latency and low cost for simple text classification. What should you choose?
o: A small language model (SLM) such as Phi
A provisioned throughput deployment of a large model
questions.e: Small models are cheaper and faster and often good enough for focused tasks.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
o: Embeddings represent text as vectors of numbers.
A higher temperature produces more varied responses.
A language model always looks up facts in a live database before answering.
questions.e: Embeddings are numeric vectors; higher temperature increases randomness; LLMs predict text and can hallucinate unless grounded.

questions.q: You must process 2 million product reviews overnight at the lowest cost, and results are not needed in real time. Which deployment type fits BEST?
o: Standard (regional) with a high rate limit
questions.e: Batch deployments process large asynchronous jobs at a lower price.

questions.q: Your application has very high, steady traffic and needs guaranteed throughput and predictable latency. Which deployment type?
questions.e: Provisioned deployments reserve capacity for predictable performance.

questions.q: A European bank requires that prompts are processed only within the EU, while still paying per token. Which deployment type?
questions.e: Data Zone deployments keep processing within a geographic zone such as the EU.

questions.q: Match each need to the model capability.
o: Describe a photo and answer questions about it
Create a poster from a description
Solve multi-step maths and logic problems
questions.e: Image understanding needs image input; creating images needs an image-generation model; complex reasoning suits reasoning models; similarity search uses embeddings.

questions.q: Which parameter restricts sampling to the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches a threshold?
questions.e: Top-p (nucleus sampling) chooses from the top tokens adding up to p.

questions.q: What usually replaces the temperature setting on reasoning models such as the o-series or GPT-5 family?
questions.e: Reasoning models expose reasoning effort instead of temperature.

questions.q: Which TWO factors should you compare when choosing between models in the Foundry model catalog for a new chatbot? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
o: Whether the model is available in your region and deployment type
The colour scheme of the model card
The number of people who starred the model on GitHub only
The length of the model name
questions.e: Capability, quality, cost, latency and regional availability drive model choice.

questions.q: What is a hallucination in generative AI?
o: A response that sounds confident but is factually wrong or unsupported
A response blocked by a content filter
A slow response caused by rate limits
questions.e: Hallucinations are plausible but false outputs.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: To tell the model to stop generating when it outputs "END", you configure a ______.
questions.e: A stop sequence ends generation when it appears.

questions.q: A marketing team wants software that drafts personalised campaign emails from a short brief. Which AI workload is this?
questions.e: Creating new text content is generative AI.

questions.q: An assistant must check an order in the ERP system, decide if a refund is allowed, issue it and email the customer. Which workload BEST fits?
questions.e: Multi-step goals with tool calls and actions call for an agent.

questions.q: A logistics company wants to read the text on shipping labels in photos. Which workload?
questions.e: Reading text in images is optical character recognition, a vision capability.

questions.q: Match each scenario to the AI workload.
o: Detect the sentiment of product reviews
Pull totals and dates out of invoices
Create an illustration for a blog post
questions.e: Audio → speech; opinions in text → text analysis; fields from documents → information extraction; new images → generative AI.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
o: An agent can call tools such as file search or custom functions.
Generating a product description from bullet points requires an agent.
Speech synthesis converts text into spoken audio.
questions.e: Agents use tools; simple generation needs only a model and prompt; synthesis = text to speech.

questions.q: A bank wants employees to ask questions in natural language and get answers from its 300-page policy manual. Which solution is MOST appropriate?
o: A generative AI app grounded on the manual (or an agent with file search)
questions.e: Grounding a model on documents (RAG) answers questions from your own content.

questions.q: Which workload describes software that recognises products on supermarket shelves and their positions?
questions.e: Locating objects in images is object detection.

questions.q: Which TWO scenarios are good fits for agentic AI rather than a simple chat completion? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
o: Booking a service appointment by checking a calendar API and confirming by email
Investigating a payment failure by querying transaction logs and opening a ticket
Rewriting a paragraph in a more formal tone
Translating a single sentence into French
Summarising a short article pasted into the prompt
questions.e: Agents fit tasks needing tools, data lookups and actions over several steps.

questions.q: A call centre needs live subtitles during calls for hearing-impaired staff. Which workload?
questions.e: Converting live audio into text is speech recognition.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: Identifying the language of incoming emails is a ______ task.
questions.e: Language detection is a text analysis capability.

questions.q: An insurer wants to extract the claim number, incident date and damage description from claim forms and from photos of damaged cars. Which workload?
questions.e: Pulling structured fields from documents and images is information extraction.

questions.q: Which workload would you use to produce a spoken weather update from a text forecast?
questions.e: Text to audio is speech synthesis.

questions.q: A retailer is planning AI features. For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
o: Generating new marketing images is an image-generation workload.
Counting customers in a store from CCTV is a text analysis workload.
Summarising thousands of reviews into themes can use text analysis or generative AI.
questions.e: Image creation = image generation; counting people = vision (object detection); summarising text = text analysis or generative AI.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a generative AI chat app and an AI agent?
o: An agent can plan and use tools to take actions; a chat app only responds with generated content
A chat app always uses more tokens
An agent cannot use a language model
A chat app can only process images
questions.e: Agents add tools, knowledge and multi-step reasoning on top of a model.

questions.q: Which text analysis technique identifies "Mumbai" as a Location and "Infosys" as an Organization?
questions.e: NER finds entities and assigns categories.

questions.q: Which technique returns the main talking points of a review, such as "delivery delay" and "refund"?
questions.e: Key phrase extraction returns the main phrases.

questions.q: A review says "The rates are great but the app is terrible." What overall sentiment label is MOST likely?
questions.e: One positive and one negative sentence gives a mixed document sentiment.

questions.q: For each statement about text analysis, select Yes if it is true.
o: Sentiment analysis returns confidence scores for positive, neutral and negative.
PII detection can return a redacted version of the text.
Key phrase extraction translates text into another language.
questions.e: Sentiment includes confidence scores; PII detection returns redacted text; translation is a separate capability.

questions.q: You must hide phone numbers and PAN numbers in chat logs before analysts read them. Which capability?
questions.e: PII detection identifies personal data and can redact it.

questions.q: Which technique tells you that customers are positive about "staff" but negative about "waiting time" in the same review?
questions.e: Opinion mining gives sentiment for specific aspects.

questions.q: Match each requirement to the text analysis technique.
o: Shorten a long complaint into two sentences
Find which language a message is written in
Link "Mercury" to the correct encyclopedia entry
Classify a review as positive or negative
questions.e: Each technique returns a different kind of insight from text.

questions.q: What is the difference between extractive and abstractive summarisation?
o: Extractive selects key sentences from the text; abstractive writes new sentences
Extractive works only on audio; abstractive only on images
questions.e: Extractive copies important sentences; abstractive generates a new summary.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: "Ravi visited Pune on 3 May" → Ravi (Person), Pune (Location), 3 May (DateTime) is the output of ______.
questions.e: NER returns entities with categories.

questions.q: Which Azure capability translates customer chats between Hindi and English?
questions.e: Translation converts text between languages.

questions.q: Which TWO outputs can Azure Language return for a document? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
o: A sentiment label with confidence scores
A list of entities with categories
A generated image of the document
An audio file of the text
questions.e: Language returns text insights such as sentiment and entities.

questions.q: Which capability converts a recorded customer call into text?
questions.e: Speech recognition turns audio into text.

questions.q: Which markup language controls pauses, speaking rate and pronunciation in synthesised speech?
questions.e: SSML controls prosody, breaks, emphasis and say-as.

questions.q: For each statement about Azure Speech, select Yes if it is true.
o: Neural voices produce natural-sounding synthesised speech.
Speech translation can turn spoken English into Hindi text or audio.
Speech synthesis transcribes meetings into text.
questions.e: Neural voices are natural; speech translation works across languages; transcription is recognition, not synthesis.

questions.q: A company wants to separate the agent’s and the customer’s words in a call transcript. Which feature?
questions.e: Diarisation identifies who spoke when.

questions.q: You need to transcribe 10,000 hours of archived call recordings. Which approach is MOST suitable?
questions.e: Batch transcription handles large volumes of recorded audio asynchronously.

questions.q: Recognition of product names like "Contoso SuperSaver Plus" is poor. What improves it?
o: Custom speech (domain-specific training or phrase lists)
questions.e: Custom speech adapts recognition to your vocabulary.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: A voice assistant typically chains speech-to-text, a language model, and ______.
questions.e: The reply is spoken back with speech synthesis.

questions.q: Which scenario is speech synthesis?
o: Reading account balances aloud to visually impaired customers
Creating captions for a live webinar
Detecting the language of an email
questions.e: Synthesis turns text into audio.

questions.q: Which capability returns objects in an image together with bounding boxes?
questions.e: Detection gives what and where.

questions.q: A model returns "A man riding a scooter on a wet street at night." What capability is this?
questions.e: A sentence describing the scene is a caption.

questions.q: For each statement about image-generation models, select Yes if it is true.
o: They can create new images from a text prompt.
They always render long text inside images accurately.
Content filters can block some prompts or outputs.
questions.e: Generation creates images; text rendering is unreliable; safety filters apply.

questions.q: You need to label each X-ray image as "fracture" or "no fracture" without locating anything. Which capability?
questions.e: One label for the whole image is classification.

questions.q: Match each requirement to the vision capability.
o: Read the amount written on a cheque
Count cars in a parking lot with their positions
Write alt text for a website image
Answer "Is the helmet strap fastened?" about a photo
questions.e: Each capability returns a different kind of output from an image.

questions.q: Which request is an image-generation model unlikely to fulfil because of responsible AI policies?
o: A realistic image of a named celebrity endorsing a product
A flat illustration of a family saving money
A product mock-up with pastel colours
questions.e: Deceptive images of real people are blocked by policy and content filters.

questions.q: Which type of model can answer a question about the contents of a photo in natural language?
o: A multimodal model that accepts image input
questions.e: Multimodal models take images and text in the prompt.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: Changing only the masked area of an existing image (for example replacing the background) is called ______.
questions.e: Editing a masked region is inpainting.

questions.q: A company wants the invoice number, vendor and total from scanned invoices as structured data. Which approach?
o: Information extraction with Azure Content Understanding
questions.e: Content Understanding extracts typed fields from documents.

questions.q: What can be extracted from a video with Content Understanding?
o: Transcripts, key frames, segment descriptions and custom fields
questions.e: Content Understanding analyses video into structured outputs.

questions.q: For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
o: Information can be extracted from audio recordings as well as documents.
Extraction results can include confidence scores.
Information extraction only works on typed text, not scans.
questions.e: Audio, images, video and scanned documents are all supported; results carry confidence scores.

questions.q: Which is a typical field to extract from a call-centre recording?
o: Whether the customer requested a refund
The bounding box of the caller’s face
The resolution of the recording device screen
The colour of the agent’s shirt
questions.e: Audio analyzers can extract facts such as intents and outcomes.

questions.q: Match each content type to an example of extracted information.
c: Products visible and whether the shelf is full
questions.e: Each modality yields its own structured fields.

questions.q: Why is extracting to a schema better than asking a chatbot "what is in this file?" for automation?
o: It produces consistent, typed fields that downstream systems can process
It does not need any model
questions.e: A schema gives predictable, machine-readable output.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: In Content Understanding, the configuration that defines what to extract and how is called an ______.
questions.e: An analyzer holds the processing settings and field schema.

questions.q: An expense app must read merchant, date and total from photographed receipts. Which capability?
o: Information extraction from images and documents
questions.e: Receipts are documents/images; extraction returns the fields.

questions.q: Where should you place the rule "Never ask the customer for their OTP" in a chat application?
o: In every user prompt typed by customers
questions.e: The system prompt sets rules for the whole conversation.

questions.q: You include three example inputs with their desired outputs before the real input. What technique is this?
questions.e: Examples in the prompt are few-shot prompting.

questions.q: For each statement about prompts, select Yes if it is true.
o: Specifying the output format (for example JSON with named keys) improves consistency.
User prompts are written by the application developer to define the persona.
Providing relevant context in the prompt can improve accuracy.
questions.e: Format instructions help; the persona belongs in the system prompt written by the developer; context improves accuracy.

questions.q: Which role in a chat conversation carries the model’s earlier replies when you send history back?
questions.e: Earlier model responses are assistant messages.

questions.q: In the Foundry portal, what must you create before an application can call a model from the catalog?
questions.e: Models are called through deployments.

questions.q: You are testing a deployed model and want starter Python code with your endpoint and deployment name. Which playground option helps?
questions.e: View code shows a ready-made sample.

questions.q: A company wants a chatbot that answers from its quarterly-updated fee schedule without retraining. What should you use?
questions.e: Grounding retrieves current documents at query time.

questions.q: Match each prompt element to its purpose.
o: “Reply in JSON with keys name and amount”
questions.e: Good system prompts combine role, format, examples and safe fallbacks.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: When deploying a model, the ______ is the value your code passes as the model parameter.
questions.e: Code calls the deployment name you chose.

questions.q: Which deployment setting limits how many tokens per minute an application can consume?
questions.e: TPM quota controls throughput.

questions.q: Which TWO practices make a prompt more effective? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
o: State the audience and the desired length
Provide the relevant source text the answer should be based on
Use as few words as possible, even if unclear
Ask several unrelated tasks in one sentence
questions.e: Clear tasks, audiences, lengths and context improve output.

questions.q: What is the difference between grounding and fine-tuning?
o: Grounding adds knowledge at query time; fine-tuning further trains the model to change its behaviour
Fine-tuning is done in the prompt; grounding retrains the model
questions.e: RAG injects data at runtime; fine-tuning adjusts model weights.

questions.q: Where in Foundry do you compare models on quality, cost and speed before deploying?
o: The model catalog and its leaderboards / compare view
questions.e: The catalog shows model cards and comparison leaderboards.

questions.q: You deploy a chat model in Foundry. For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
o: You can test prompts in the chat playground without writing code.
Content filter settings can be applied to the deployment.
The deployment can be used only from the portal, not from code.
questions.e: Playgrounds allow no-code testing; guardrails attach to deployments; deployments are callable from code.

questions.q: Which Python package provides AIProjectClient for working with a Microsoft Foundry project?
questions.e: The Foundry SDK client library is azure-ai-projects.

questions.q: Complete the code: client = project.______() returns an OpenAI-compatible client for calling deployed models.
questions.e: AIProjectClient.get_openai_client() returns the OpenAI client.

questions.q: Which credential class lets the same Python code authenticate with your Azure CLI sign-in locally and with a managed identity in Azure?
questions.e: DefaultAzureCredential tries several Entra ID sources in order.

questions.q: What is the format of a Foundry project endpoint used with AIProjectClient?
questions.e: Project endpoints end with /api/projects/<project-name>.

questions.q: Your chat app answers the second question as if the first was never asked. What is the MOST likely cause?
o: The app does not send the conversation history (or previous_response_id)
The deployment type is Global Standard
The system prompt is too short
questions.e: Models are stateless; history must be sent or chained.

questions.q: For each statement about the Responses API, select Yes if it is true.
o: previous_response_id can chain a follow-up to an earlier response.
The model parameter takes the Azure subscription ID.
questions.e: output_text holds the reply; previous_response_id keeps context; model takes the deployment name.

questions.q: Your app receives HTTP 429 errors during peak usage. What should it do?
o: Retry with exponential backoff and consider increasing the deployment’s rate limit
Switch to a different subscription for every request
questions.e: 429 means rate limited; back off and retry.

questions.q: A call returns HTTP 404 with "DeploymentNotFound". What should you check first?
o: That the model parameter matches the deployment name exactly
The size of the system prompt
The colour theme of the portal
questions.e: A wrong deployment name causes 404 errors.

questions.q: Which property of a response tells you how many tokens were consumed?
questions.e: usage includes input, output and total tokens.

questions.q: Match each code element to its purpose in a Foundry chat client.
c: Get a client for model calls
Send a prompt and get a response
Read the endpoint and settings from a .env file
questions.e: These four lines form the core of every Foundry chat client.

questions.q: Where should you store the API key for a lab chat app?
o: In a .env file excluded from source control (or Azure Key Vault)
questions.e: Secrets must not be committed to code repositories.

questions.q: Which role assignment is commonly needed for a developer using keyless authentication to call models and agents in a Foundry project?
o: Azure AI User on the project or resource
questions.e: Foundry RBAC roles such as Azure AI User grant data-plane access.

questions.q: Which TWO approaches keep context across turns in a chat app built with the Responses API? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
o: Send the full list of previous messages as input
Pass previous_response_id with the follow-up request
Create a new deployment for each turn
questions.e: Either send history or let the service chain responses.

questions.q: In the Chat Completions API, where is the generated text found?
questions.e: Chat Completions returns choices with messages.

questions.q: Complete the code to give the model its persona: client.responses.create(model=MODEL, ______="You are a bank FAQ assistant.", input=question)
questions.e: The instructions parameter acts as the system prompt in the Responses API.

questions.q: Why should a long-running chat app trim or summarise old turns?
o: To stay within the context window and control token cost
To make the model more creative
Because Foundry deletes history after 3 turns
questions.e: Every turn resends history tokens.

questions.q: For each statement about authentication, select Yes if it is true.
o: Keyless authentication uses Microsoft Entra ID tokens instead of an API key.
API keys should be rotated if they are exposed.
DefaultAzureCredential requires the API key to be hard-coded.
questions.e: Entra ID is keyless; leaked keys must be rotated; DefaultAzureCredential uses identities, not keys.

questions.q: Which Python framework is suggested in the course for a quick web front end for a chat client?
questions.e: Streamlit builds simple chat UIs quickly.

questions.q: A request fails with an error indicating the content was filtered. What happened?
o: The prompt or response triggered the deployment’s content safety filters
questions.e: Content filters block harmful prompts or outputs.

questions.q: Which statement about the OpenAI client returned by get_openai_client() is correct?
o: It calls models deployed in your Foundry project using OpenAI-style APIs
It can only call models hosted by OpenAI.com
It is used to manage Azure subscriptions
questions.e: Foundry exposes OpenAI-compatible APIs for deployed models.

questions.q: Which components make up an agent in Microsoft Foundry?
o: A model, instructions, tools and knowledge
Only a model and an API key
A speech voice and an SSML file
A resource group and a region
questions.e: Agents combine a model with instructions, tools and knowledge.

questions.q: An agent must answer questions using a 200-page product manual. Which tool should you add?
questions.e: File search indexes uploaded documents in a vector store.

questions.q: Users ask an agent to calculate EMIs and produce a chart from a CSV of loans. Which tool should you add?
questions.e: Code interpreter runs Python for calculations, charts and file analysis.

questions.q: An agent must create a ticket in your company’s ticketing system. Which tool type allows this?
o: A function (or OpenAPI) tool that calls your code or API
questions.e: Function calling lets the agent request actions implemented by your code.

questions.q: For each statement about Foundry agents, select Yes if it is true.
o: You can create and test an agent in the Foundry portal without writing code.
An agent’s instructions act like a system prompt.
Agents cannot be called from a Python application.
questions.e: Agents are built and tested in the portal and called from client apps.

questions.q: Complete the code: conversation = openai.______.create() creates an object that keeps an agent’s multi-turn history.
questions.e: Conversations store the messages for multi-turn chat.

questions.q: How does the Python client in the course bind its OpenAI client to a specific agent?
questions.e: Passing agent_name returns a client pre-bound to that agent.

questions.q: Which class defines a prompt-based agent when creating it with the azure-ai-projects SDK?
questions.e: agents.create_version takes a PromptAgentDefinition with model and instructions.

questions.q: Match each agent requirement to the tool.
o: Look up a live order status in your API
Search a large enterprise index you already maintain
questions.e: Choose tools by the data source and action needed.

questions.q: What happens each time you save changes to an agent in Foundry?
o: A new agent version is created
questions.e: Agents are versioned so changes can be tracked and rolled back.

questions.q: Which TWO are advantages of using an agent instead of a simple chat client? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
o: The agent can call tools such as file search and code interpreter
It never needs a model deployment
questions.e: Agents add managed state and tools, but still use models and tokens.

questions.q: When testing an agent in the playground, where can you see which tool it used to answer?
o: In the run details / trace for the response
questions.e: Traces show tool calls and steps.

questions.q: Which statement BEST describes when to build an agent rather than a chat app?
o: When the task needs data lookups, calculations or actions across multiple steps
Whenever the user writes in English
When you want the lowest possible latency for a one-line reply
questions.e: Agents are for tool use and multi-step tasks.

questions.q: A support agent uses file search over a policy PDF. For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
o: The policy content is chunked and stored in a vector store.
The agent can quote the relevant section in its answer.
File search lets the agent execute Python code.
questions.e: File search indexes documents for retrieval; running code is code interpreter.

questions.q: Which instruction makes a customer support agent safer?
o: “Never request OTPs, PINs or full card numbers.”
“Always answer, even if you are unsure.”
questions.e: Explicit safety rules in instructions reduce risk.

questions.q: Complete the code: agent = project.agents.______(agent_name="support-agent", definition=PromptAgentDefinition(model=MODEL, instructions=TEXT))
questions.e: create_version creates or updates an agent version.

questions.q: Your agent answers a follow-up question ("Can it be waived?") correctly in context. Why?
o: Both requests used the same conversation ID
questions.e: The conversation keeps the earlier messages.

questions.q: An agent should get approval from a human before issuing refunds above ₹10,000. Which responsible AI principle does this support?
questions.e: Human approval of high-impact actions keeps people accountable.

questions.q: Which Foundry capability hosts agents, runs the model-tool loop and stores conversations?
questions.e: The Agent Service runs and manages agents.

questions.q: Which TWO steps are part of building the customer support agent in the course? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
o: Write instructions that restrict answers to the policy document
Upload the policy document as knowledge with file search
questions.e: Instructions plus file-search knowledge ground the support agent.

questions.q: Which Python client class analyses sentiment with Azure Language in Foundry Tools?
questions.e: azure-ai-textanalytics provides TextAnalyticsClient.

questions.q: Complete the code to get aspect-level results: client.analyze_sentiment(docs, ______=True)
questions.e: show_opinion_mining returns targets and assessments.

questions.q: Which endpoint do you use for Azure Language and Azure Speech in your Foundry resource?
o: The resource endpoint (without /api/projects/...) with its key or Entra ID
questions.e: Foundry Tools use the resource endpoint.

questions.q: Which Speech SDK object holds the key and region (or endpoint) used to connect?
questions.e: SpeechConfig encapsulates connection information.

questions.q: Which property sets the voice for speech synthesis?
questions.e: speech_synthesis_voice_name selects a neural voice.

questions.q: For each statement about the Speech SDK, select Yes if it is true.
o: AudioOutputConfig can write synthesised audio to a file.
recognize_once is designed for transcribing hour-long recordings.
questions.e: recognize_once handles a single short utterance; use continuous or batch transcription for long audio.

questions.q: After calling recognize_once_async().get(), how do you confirm speech was recognised?
questions.e: The reason property indicates success or no match.

questions.q: You want an MP3 file instead of the default WAV output from text-to-speech. What should you configure?
questions.e: set_speech_synthesis_output_format chooses MP3, WAV and others.

questions.q: A deployed multimodal model should answer a customer’s recorded question directly. How do you send the recording?
o: As an input_audio content part with base64 data and its format
As a URL in the system prompt only
questions.e: Speech-capable models accept input_audio in messages.

questions.q: Match each Azure Language method to its result.
questions.e: Each method returns a different text insight.

questions.q: Which method returns an abstractive summary of long documents with Azure Language?
questions.e: Summarisation is a long-running operation started with begin_* methods.

questions.q: Which TWO are valid reasons to use Azure Speech rather than a multimodal model for a voice app? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
o: You need specific neural voices and SSML control
You need batch transcription of large recorded archives
You need a model with a larger context window
You want to avoid any authentication
questions.e: Azure Speech provides fine control over voices, SSML and batch transcription.

questions.q: In the Lab 4 pipeline, what is the correct order?
o: Speech-to-text → sentiment and key phrases → reply generation → text-to-speech
questions.e: Transcribe first, analyse the text, then speak the reply.

questions.q: Complete the SSML so an OTP is read digit by digit: 4821
questions.e: interpret-as="characters" spells out each digit.

questions.q: Each Azure Language result can represent an error for one document. What should production code check?
o: The is_error property of each result before reading fields
questions.e: Per-document errors are flagged with is_error.

questions.q: You build a text-analysis app. For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
o: Results are returned in the same order as the input documents.
You can authenticate with AzureKeyCredential or DefaultAzureCredential.
Azure Language requires a deployed image-generation model.
questions.e: Results keep input order; key or Entra ID authentication works; no image model is needed.

questions.q: Which recognition method should you use for a live meeting that lasts an hour?
questions.e: Continuous recognition processes ongoing audio with events.

questions.q: In a Responses API request, which content part type sends an image to a multimodal model?
questions.e: Images are sent as input_image parts with a URL or data URL.

questions.q: What format can you use to send a local image file to a multimodal model?
o: A base64 data URL such as data:image/jpeg;base64,...
questions.e: Encode the image in base64 as a data URL.

questions.q: Your captioning app uses a text-only model deployment and fails to describe images. What should you change?
o: Deploy and use a model that supports image input
questions.e: Image interpretation requires a multimodal model.

questions.q: Complete the code to create an image: client.images.______(model=IMAGE_DEPLOYMENT, prompt=text, size="1024x1024")
questions.e: images.generate creates images from a prompt.

questions.q: An image-generation response contains data[0].b64_json. What do you do with it?
o: Decode the base64 string and save it as an image file
Use it as an API key
questions.e: The image is returned as base64-encoded bytes.

questions.q: For each statement about image generation in Foundry, select Yes if it is true.
o: You can try image models in the Images playground before writing code.
Prompts and outputs pass through content filters.
Image generation models are the best choice for reading text on receipts.
questions.e: Playgrounds and filters apply; reading receipts is a vision/extraction task.

questions.q: A user asks a follow-up question about an image already discussed. How does the app keep the image in context?
o: It keeps the earlier messages (including the image) in the conversation history
questions.e: Models are stateless; history carries the image and earlier answers.

questions.q: Match each task to the deployed model type.
o: Answer "what is the total?" about a receipt photo
Produce a portrait-format banner from text
questions.e: Understanding images needs image input; creating images needs an image-generation model.

questions.q: Which size value requests a landscape image from GPT-Image-1?
questions.e: 1536x1024 is landscape; 1024x1536 is portrait.

questions.q: Your image request fails with an HTTP 400 error mentioning content policy. What is the BEST way to handle it in the app?
o: Catch the error and show a friendly message asking the user to change the prompt
Retry the same prompt in a loop
questions.e: Content-filter rejections should be handled gracefully.

questions.q: Which TWO prompt elements usually improve generated images? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
o: A clear style, for example "flat vector illustration"
Composition and colour details, for example "wide shot, warm sunset colours"
A request for exact long paragraphs of text in the image
questions.e: Style, composition and lighting guide image models.

questions.q: Besides the images API, how else can an application or agent generate images in Foundry?
o: By using the image_generation tool with the Responses API or an agent
questions.e: Image generation is available as a tool in Responses and agents.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: Provenance metadata showing an image is AI-generated is known as ______.
questions.e: Content credentials (C2PA) add provenance information.

questions.q: Which combination does the Lab 5 app use?
o: A multimodal chat deployment for descriptions and an image deployment for generation
One embedding model for both tasks
questions.e: Understanding and creating images need different model types.

questions.q: Which service in Foundry Tools extracts structured fields from documents, images, audio and video?
questions.e: Content Understanding handles multimodal extraction.

questions.q: What defines the fields, types and descriptions a custom analyzer extracts?
o: The system prompt of a chat deployment
questions.e: Analyzers use a field schema.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: After POSTing to an analyzer’s analyze endpoint you receive HTTP 202 and must poll the URL in the ______ header.
questions.e: Analysis is asynchronous; poll the Operation-Location URL.

questions.q: Which prebuilt analyzer ID is used for invoices in the course?
questions.e: prebuilt-invoice extracts standard invoice fields.

questions.q: For each statement about Content Understanding results, select Yes if it is true.
o: Each extracted field can include a confidence score.
Document results can include markdown text and tables.
Results are always returned synchronously in the first response.
questions.e: Fields include confidence; documents include markdown and tables; analysis is asynchronous.

questions.q: Match each field to the best method.
o: IsOverdue inferred from the due date
questions.e: Extract copies values; classify picks from a list; generate infers.

questions.q: What status indicates a Content Understanding job has finished successfully?
questions.e: Poll until status is Succeeded (or Failed).

questions.q: What must be true of a file URL you send to the analyze endpoint?
o: The service must be able to read it, for example a public URL or a Blob URL with a SAS token
It must be a local C:\ path
It must be shorter than 10 characters
It must point to a GitHub profile page
questions.e: The service downloads the input from the URL.

questions.q: How should an invoice pipeline handle fields with low confidence scores?
o: Route them to a human reviewer before posting to accounting
questions.e: Human review keeps the process reliable and accountable.

questions.q: Which TWO outputs can Content Understanding return for a video? Each correct answer is a complete solution.
o: Key frames returned as image URLs
A transcript of the spoken audio
questions.e: Video analysis returns frames, transcripts, segments and fields.

questions.q: Where in the result JSON are the extracted fields for the first input found?
questions.e: Fields are inside each contents entry.

questions.q: Before using Content Understanding Studio for the first time, what must be configured on your Foundry resource?
o: Default model deployments (for example with autodeployment enabled)
questions.e: Content Understanding uses default model deployments behind the scenes.

questions.q: A company wants to analyse support-call recordings. For each statement, select Yes if it is true.
o: A Content Understanding audio analyzer can return a transcript.
Custom fields such as RefundRequested can be defined.
Audio must first be converted into an image.
questions.e: Audio analyzers transcribe and extract custom fields directly.

questions.q: A field in the result has type "array". Which property holds its items?
questions.e: Typed values use properties such as valueString, valueNumber, valueObject and valueArray.
